episodes.title: ChatGPT Temporary Chat Isn't Instant Deletion #Shorts
episodes.source_linked_claims: OpenAI official help center; original fictional demo, not a real ChatGPT account
scenes: Temporary Chat stays out of your history while it remains temporary, but that does not mean zero retention.
OpenAI says an unsaved temporary chat may be retained up to thirty days for safety purposes.
While it remains temporary, OpenAI says it is not used to improve models and does not create memories.
If you save a temporary chat, it becomes a regular chat with different history and retention rules.
Temporary can be useful for privacy, but still avoid sharing information you don't want stored anywhere.

episodes.title: AI Quoted a Document? Check Those EXACT Words #Shorts
episodes.source_linked_claims: OpenAI official help center; original fictional demo, not a real ChatGPT account
scenes: An AI assistant can produce a convincing quotation that is not actually present in the source document.
OpenAI notes that chat models can make incorrect or misleading claims even when the answer sounds confident.
Search the original document for the quoted phrase. Confirm that the words and surrounding context match.
In this fictional example, the summary changes a number. Verify the exact figure before repeating it.
If you cannot find the passage, label it unverified rather than presenting AI-generated wording as a direct quote.

episodes.title: AI Answer Looks Convincing? Verify the Actual Evidence in 5 Steps
episodes.source_linked_claims: OpenAI official help center; original fictional demo, not a real ChatGPT account
scenes: An AI answer looks polished and confident. In this fictional example, it reports fifty when the source says fifteen. The design looks convincing, but the important number changed. Here's a verification workflow.

Modern chat models produce useful language, but they can still invent facts, citations, or quotations. OpenAI's own help explains these limitations. A helpful draft is not the same as independent verification.

Start by opening the original source rather than trusting a link label. Is it a real publication, and does it discuss the claim you want to repeat? Check that the page belongs to the organization being cited.
Find the exact sentence or passage supporting the answer. A real web page can be cited for the wrong claim. If the sentence is missing, do not turn the source's reputation into imaginary evidence.

Next compare numbers, units, dates, and definitions. A tiny numeric change can invert a financial or scientific conclusion. Keep figures from the original document alongside the AI draft for comparison.

Look for words like may, can, often, and depends. An AI summary that turns may into always overstates the evidence. In this fictional example, the source describes a possibility, not a universal result.
Read at least the surrounding paragraph. An extracted sentence may omit a condition or exception. Verify what population, product version, or date the source discusses before sharing a claim.
A link that returns an error, a mismatched title, or a source that never mentioned the topic is a warning. Search the publication's official pages and avoid inventing a supporting citation.
Direct quotations need exact words. If a phrase cannot be located in the source, rewrite it as your own summary only after verifying the actual meaning. Do not present it in quotation marks.

For software settings, start with the product's current official documentation. Menu names and features can change, so note the supported platform and version rather than treating a screenshot as permanent proof.

Now separate claims into verified, uncertain, and unsupported. You can still use AI to explain a complex topic, but keep uncertainty visible and avoid giving an unverified answer more certainty than its source warrants.

Before posting a tutorial or citing a result: open the source, locate the claim, compare numbers, preserve qualifiers, and read the surrounding context. Ask which step would have caught the fictional fifty versus fifteen error.
